values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, not within 300 ft of any lake or facility. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs'; Thompson's ridge-top tract is reached on the unimproved Fire Trail.

summary: Confirmed no hookups and no water/dump/restrooms (DWR: no amenities), and the 14-night limit with the $10 camping authorization. Thompson's own page says nothing about camping beyond linking DWR's statewide rules; it lists 11 designated parking areas and an unimproved Fire Trail to the ridge-top tract. Not stated on DWR pages: season, the $4 access-permit price (left to the inherited all-in rate and the AWH-confirmed note), any Thompson-specific RV restriction. Existing groups without provenance left unchanged except where DWR states them.
